name: CBR250R MC41, Keihin software KYJA203 (38770-KYJ-922 / -971)
notes: Sources: our own search of the stock 922/971 images and the HondaDLC logs (2026-10-27), and the TunerPro XDF 'CBR250R_cbrlocal_testing' by cbrlocal (cbr250.net, 2023-10-27; copy in reference/). Confidence: 'confirmed' = checked on the bike, 'likely' = two independent sources agree, 'guess' = one source or shape only. Never add a table without evidence.

rpm.evidence: Ours: x 18000/65536 gives round rpm 800, 1000 ... 10,500. XDF: same address, X*7/25.485 (the same scale).

tps.evidence: Ours: 0-1023 (10-bit TPS). XDF: same address, X/10.23 = % (gives round 0, 1, 2 ... 50, 60, 70, 100 %).

map.evidence: Ours: 22 bytes 0-255 after the TPS axis. XDF: same address, MAP axis, X*3.8 mbar (0-97 kPa).

tables.name: Fuel A (primary)
tables.evidence: Ours: 29 x 22 words, rising with load. XDF: same address, 'Speed Density, mBar vs RPM, the primary fuel table', X*0.0008 (ms). Axis disagreement: the XDF says MAP, but the HondaDLC logs fit throttle far better (logged injector time vs this map: r = 0.80 on throttle, 0.41 on MAP). Use 'columns' to switch.

tables.name: Fuel B (secondary)
tables.evidence: Ours: 29 x 22 words after fuel A. XDF: same address, 'Alpha-N, the secondary fuel table', throttle axis, X*0.0008. Logs: r = 0.80 on throttle, 0.45 on MAP. When the ECU uses A vs B is not known.

tables.name: Ignition, in gear
tables.evidence: Ours: 29 x 22 bytes, rises with rpm, falls with load. XDF: same address, 'Ignition Timing Gears 1-6', throttle axis, X*0.355-15.71 deg (scale not checked: compare idle with the workshop manual's ignition timing spec). Logs (bike in neutral): r = 0.93 on throttle.

tables.name: Ignition, neutral
tables.evidence: Ours: same shape after ignition A; the only table that differs 922 vs 971 (0xAD40-0xADA0). XDF: same address, 'Ignition Timing Neutral', X*0.355-15.71. Logs (bike on the stand, in neutral): r = 0.96 on throttle, the best fit of the four maps, which supports the 'neutral' label.

tables.name: Rev limiter
tables.evidence: XDF only: 'Rev Limiter', fuel enable / fuel cut, X/3.64089. Stock 10,300 / 10,500 rpm in both images.

tables.name: O2 closed loop: lower throttle limit
tables.evidence: XDF only: 'Lower Throttle Angle: closed loop is active above this percent'. Stock 3.5 % at every rpm.

tables.name: O2 closed loop: upper throttle limit
tables.evidence: XDF only: 'Upper Throttle Angle: open loop is activated above this throttle percent'. Stock 30 % (18.5 % in the 2,000 rpm entry). So the O2 sensor trims the fuel between about 3.5 % and 30 % throttle.

tables.name: Fault code list
tables.evidence: XDF: 'DTCs' at this address. Ours: the pairs are exactly the workshop manual's codes (1-1, 1-2, 7-1 ... 21-1, 23-1, 29-1, 54-1, 54-2), with 0-0 in the unused slots. There is no PAIR code in the list. Edited only through the off-road options.

options.name: O2 sensor closed loop off
options.note: Sets the upper throttle limit to 0 % at every rpm, so the ECU stays in open loop (map only). Source: the XDF's description of the limit tables; not yet tested on an ECU.

options.name: O2 sensor + heater fault codes off (21-1, 23-1)
options.note: Only if the sensor is removed. Blanks the two codes in the fault code list to 0-0, like the unused slots. Guess: test on the spare ECU first.

options.name: PAIR (air injection) off
options.note: The ECU's fault code list has no PAIR code, so unplugging the solenoid and fitting block-off plates probably needs no map change. Check the workshop manual's PAIR wiring to be sure.

options.name: Bank angle fault codes off (54-1, 54-2)
options.note: The sensor is missing on this bike. Fitting one is the better fix: it cuts the engine if the bike falls over. Guess: test on the spare ECU first.
